title: Friendship kept up

lines: A NAME THAT USED TO BE A DAILY CALL.
A HOUSEPLANT ON A HIGH SHELF.
cards: Somewhere in a phone there's a name that used to be a daily call. Nobody fought. Nobody decided anything.
One of you moved, or had a baby, or changed jobs, and the calls became texts, the texts became birthday messages, and then one year even the birthday slipped by.
Sometimes a friendship ends like a houseplant on a high shelf: not killed, just not watered. Marriages have vows and anniversaries. Families have holidays.
Friendship mostly has nothing holding it up except the people in it.

teach.b: First, Proverbs on the old friend: "Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not." Look at the second half: not just your friend, but your father's friend, someone you inherited.
Proverbs treats an old friendship as worth keeping across a lifetime, even passed down like a family table.
Second, shew himself friendly. Another proverb, in the King James wording: "A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly." Having friends and showing friendliness are tied together.
The friendship doesn't run on its own; someone has to keep showing up.

teach.h: TO HAVE A FRIEND, BE ONE.
teach.b: Third, to have a friend, be one. Ralph Waldo Emerson, in his essay on friendship, puts it in one line: "The only way to have a friend is to be one." Emerson can be lofty about friendship, but this line is practical.
It moves the question from whether they've called lately to whether you have.

Fourth, small, often, on purpose. Tending a friendship isn't a big reunion trip. It's a short message that says I thought of you, a photo of the café you both used to sit in, a question about their mother's surgery.

And look back at the week, which has been love in practice: what we live by, win their friendship and understanding, something got watered, the hard ones too, this body, a daily choice, and now tend it.
Each one moved love from a feeling toward something done.

how: In Jewish and Christian tradition, Proverbs is read as practical wisdom about friendship; people keep friendships alive through visits, calls, letters and shared meals, sometimes around holidays and life events.

o: the author of the proverbs about an old friend
the essayist who wrote: to have a friend, be one
a poet who wrote that real friends never need tending

games.q: who said what about keeping friends — tap the pairs.
p: to have a friend is to be one

s: Proverbs says to keep only the friends you choose yourself
it also says not to forsake your father's friend.
Emerson wrote that the only way to have a friend is to be one
the line comes from his essay on friendship.
in the hook, the friendship ends with a big fight
nobody fought; it faded from not being tended.

games.q: an old friend's name comes up in your phone. it's been a year. what do you do?
o: wait for them to reach out first.
send a short message: you came to mind.
games.why: Emerson moves the question from whether they've called to whether you have: the only way to have a friend is to be one.

practice: Let a friend come to mind whom you haven't spoken to in a while, not someone who hurt you, just someone the current carried away, and stay with one specific moment you shared: a joke, a kitchen, a long drive.
Then turn Emerson's line around on yourself, and let one short, light message take shape in your mind, the kind that simply says they came to mind. If you pray, you can give thanks for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Emerson. The essayist who wrote that the only way to have a friend is to be one. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: tend it. A friendship is kept the way a plant is, with a little water, often. Day eight hundred sixty-one, done.
